ai.description: Jerdon's Kukri Snake reaches 40–50 cm. It is brownish-grey with a series of dark, light-edged dorsal blotches and a distinct V-shaped mark on the nape. It possesses enlarged, blade-like rear teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Oligodon venustus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark V-shaped or chevron-like marking on the nape of its neck, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Jerdon's Kukri Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests across the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations ranging from 600 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Oligodon venustus* is primarily nocturnal and uses its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice into the eggs of reptiles, which form a significant part of its diet.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon venustus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon venustus* is found in the Western Ghats of peninsular India, ranging from lowlands up to approximately 1,200 meters in elevation.
